text: Night. I'm building Cutlist, an AI tool that cuts a first assembly from raw footage, and the accelerator application is due in nineteen days, so I'll want help with the pitch.
Happy to help. Where is the application now?
Slide two is the problem and I've rewritten it four times. I prefer one input and one button to a settings page, and I'd rather cut a scene by a third than add a shot to explain it.
Understood. A shorter slide may serve you better, and I can suggest some friendly alternatives.
No, that's not how I work, and don't open with praise. Open with the problem.
Please be blunt with me. I don't want hype, I want the answer first and the reasons after it, in under eighty words.
Noted: answer first, reasons after, no hype, under eighty words.
One more thing about how I like my notes: short numbered steps, three at most.
Runway is eleven weeks, so every cost gets stated per hour of footage. I work alone at night around the thesis short.
I'll send the one-minute video script to the editors in the beta this Friday, so I need a draft ready before then.
Friday it is. I'll help you get the script ready.
I still can't tell whether the retention drop comes from the new auto-tagging screen or from the exam weeks, and I haven't found a way to settle it.
Costs stay per hour of footage in every slide, the runway is short.
